For AdS-Vaidya, our approach predicts a different result from earlier piecewise geodesic constructions, while reproducing the field theory answer. Across these examples, the operator ordering uniquely determines the imaginary part of the complex-valued entropy, which is quantized in units of $cπ/6$ and sensitive to the effective causal structure but not to the underlying dynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper formulates timelike entanglement entropy in 2D CFT via analytic continuation of replica twist correlators to timelike-separated insertions, generalizing to arbitrary temporal subregions. In holography, it derives complex extremal surface prescriptions via boundary-anchored complex geodesics and complex cosmic branes for Rényi index n>1. Applications to excited states and quantum quenches show agreement with bulk calculations, and for AdS-Vaidya it corrects earlier piecewise constructions. The imaginary part of the entropy is quantized in units of cπ/6 and determined by operator ordering and causal structure.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous field-theoretic foundation for timelike entanglement entropy and its holographic dual via complex extremal surfaces, generalizing recent proposals and resolving inconsistencies in earlier constructions.
AI.method: Analytic continuation of replica twist correlators in 2D CFT to timelike-separated insertions; holographic computation using semiclassical boundary correlators identifying boundary-anchored complex geodesics as bulk saddles; explicit construction of complex cosmic brane geometries for Rényi index n>1.
AI.result: Timelike entanglement entropy is formulated via analytic continuation of twist correlators; holographically dual to complex geodesics selected by smallest real part of length; complex cosmic branes constructed for n>1; operator ordering yields imaginary part quantized in units of cπ/6; AdS-Vaidya predictions differ from piecewise geodesics but match field theory.
AI.conclusion: The complex extremal surface prescription is rigorously derived from boundary CFT, applies to arbitrary temporal subregions, and reveals that the imaginary part of timelike entanglement entropy is universal (quantized) and sensitive only to causal structure, not dynamics.

title: Resurgent Lambert series from Feynman and beyond
comment: 8 pages, talk given at Loops and Legs 2026. Version accepted in Proceedings of Science (LL2026) 020
summary: Lambert series of the form $\sum_{n>0}a(n)q^n/(1-q^n)$ are ubiquitous in mathematical physics. In particular, 2-loop sunrise and 3-loop banana Feynman diagrams yield Lambert series with $a(n)$ of the form $χ(n)/n^s$ where $χ(n)$ is a Dirichlet character. Resurgence concerns the singular limit as $|q|$ approaches 1. In the Feynman cases we can control this limit, obtaining rapidly convergent expressions, since the Lambert series are iterated integrals of holomorphic Eisenstein series twisted by a character. We generalize this result, to include modular resurgent structures found in topological-string observables.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Lambert series with Dirichlet characters appearing in Feynman diagrams (sunrise/banana), showing they are iterated integrals of twisted Eisenstein series, enabling controlled asymptotic analysis near |q|→1 and generalization to modular resurgence in topological string theory.
AI.motivation: Lambert series with Dirichlet character coefficients arise ubiquitously in mathematical physics, particularly in Feynman diagram computations (2-loop sunrise, 3-loop banana). Understanding their singular limit |q|→1 (resurgence) is crucial but challenging.
AI.method: The authors identify that these Lambert series are iterated integrals of holomorphic Eisenstein series twisted by a Dirichlet character. This structural insight allows controlled treatment of the |q|→1 limit, yielding rapidly convergent expressions.
AI.result: The method provides controlled, rapidly convergent expressions for the singular limit of Feynman diagram Lambert series. The result is generalized to include modular resurgent structures appearing in topological-string observables.
AI.conclusion: Lambert series with Dirichlet character coefficients (as in Feynman diagrams) are iterated integrals of twisted Eisenstein series, enabling resurgence analysis. The framework extends to modular resurgent structures in topological string theory.
